answer: Staked peer review runs in three steps. First, each reviewer locks a bond before seeing the claim. Second, the work is split across independent auditors, so no single reviewer can wave it through. Third, spot checks reopen a sample later and a missed error costs the reviewer's bond. An inlet that carries no water silts up and a bridge with no traffic is dismantled, so idle identities bleed standing every epoch. Across the ocean of submissions the sample is small, but the chance of being sampled keeps reviewers honest.
